kicker: THE FILES · BOX SCORE · ONE NIGHT ONLY*
label: Lost the fight
title: Army vs. Emus
summary: A box score for the 1932 Emu War in Western Australia: three soldiers and two machine guns against about 20,000 emus, at 9,860 rounds for 986 birds.

blocks.text: Campion, Western Australia · Nov. 2 - Dec. 10, 1932 · Two rounds
*Two rounds, actually. The first one lasted six days.

rows: One truck. Not enough. The gunner couldn’t aim.
Nearly 50 km/h. Over rough ground, in several directions at once.

blocks.text: Source: the commanding officer’s own report. Exactly ten. We make no accusations. We just noticed.
What finally worked: bounties, farmers’ own rifles and better fences. No machine guns required.
The emus didn’t win. They just didn’t lose, which was more than the other side could say.
Please don’t send us your spreadsheet of 1932 emu counts. [E.G.] · They’re going to send the spreadsheet. [H.C.]

sources: Drawn from the Emu War feature’s sources. The 986 confirmed kills and 9,860 rounds are Major Meredith’s own figures, from his unpublished report; bird counts were estimates at the time.
Murray Johnson, “‘Feathered Foes’: Soldier Settlers and Western Australia’s ‘Emu War’ of 1932,” Journal of Australian Studies 30:88 (2006).
